definitions.gloss: to happen to be present, to be on the scene by chance
definitions.explanation: To be at a particular place when something occurs, without having planned to be there. Emphasizes the coincidental nature of one's presence.

examples.japanese: ⟦{偶然|ぐうぜん}→偶然：02674_guuzen⟧{居合|いあ}わせた⟦{医師|いし}→医師：11851_ishi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{助|たす}けた→助ける：00895_tasukeru⟧。
examples.english: A doctor who happened to be there helped.

examples.japanese: ⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{居合|いあ}わせた⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{証言|しょうげん}→証言：11088_shougen⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: A person who happened to be at the scene of the accident gave testimony.

examples.japanese: ⟦レストラン→レストラン：01048_resutoran⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦していたら→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦{有名人|ゆうめいじん}→有名人：17812_yuumeijin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{居合|いあ}わせて⟦{驚|おどろ}いた→驚く：01255_odoroku⟧。
examples.english: I was surprised to find myself in the same restaurant as a celebrity while having dinner.

notes:
Ichidan verb ({一段動詞|いちだんどうし}).
- Negative: {居合|いあ}わせない
- Polite: {居合|いあ}わせます
- Te-form: {居合|いあ}わせて
- Past: {居合|いあ}わせた

USAGE:
{居合|いあ}わせる most commonly appears in the past tense ({居合|いあ}わせた) as a relative clause modifying a person: {居合|いあ}わせた⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a person who happened to be there). It is frequently used in news reports about accidents, crimes, and emergencies.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{偶然|ぐうぜん}→偶然：02674_guuzen⟧{居合|いあ}わせる: to happen to be present by chance
- ⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{居合|いあ}わせる: to be present at the scene
- {居合|いあ}わせた⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a bystander, a person who happened to be there
